leftEvidence.title: David teaches a lament for Saul and Jonathan

points.label: Action and response
points.left: The song names Israel’s beauty, Gilboa, weapons, Saul and Jonathan together, the daughters of Israel, and Jonathan’s love.
points.right: Champions meet, battle spreads, Asahel pursues Abner and is killed, Joab continues until Abner calls for the sword to stop consuming.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places grief becomes a taught public song inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places rival kingship produces deaths David does not direct in the scene inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 1:17–27 and 2 Samuel 2:12–32 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Judah, Conflict, and Unification” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: A contest at Gibeon becomes civil bloodshed

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 1:17–27 foregrounds grief becomes a taught public song; 2 Samuel 2:12–32 foregrounds rival kingship produces deaths David does not direct in the scene. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
